findings.where: README.env-vars.md, section "How to check this file", lines 1139-1140
findings.problem: The text says: "At the baseline commit the commands print no name." That is false. The commands of the section print one name, SELF_DIR. A reviewer who runs the commands sees a name that the file calls a defect of the file.
findings.evidence: I ran the commands of the section on the checkout (baseline commit 7eddde7895 plus the staged files), with read-only git grep and grep. They found 291 distinct names. README.env-vars.md gives 851 known names. One name is printed: SELF_DIR. The source is line 7 of perfetto/launcher-common: `: "${SELF_DIR:?launcher-common must be sourced with SELF_DIR set}"`. The shell pattern of the check matches `${SELF_DIR:?`. README.env-vars.md does not hold the text SELF_DIR (grep -c gives 0). SELF_DIR is a shell variable, not an environment variable. perfetto/tronperf (line 3) and perfetto/wrapper (line 3) assign it before they load perfetto/launcher-common.
findings.fix: Replace the paragraph at lines 1139-1140 with this text: "The check treats every name in backticks in this file as known. One known name is not an environment variable: `SELF_DIR` is a shell variable. `perfetto/tronperf` and `perfetto/wrapper` assign it before they load `perfetto/launcher-common`. It is named here so that the commands do not print it. At the baseline commit the commands print no name." I checked the result: with `SELF_DIR` in the known names, the commands print 0 names.

findings.where: AGENTS.md lines 29-33 (staged section "Environment variables") against README.env-vars.md lines 73-86 ("Rules for developers")
findings.problem: AGENTS.md requires less than the rule that it points to. AGENTS.md names 3 of the 7 cases in which README.env-vars.md requires an update. It leaves out 4 cases: a reader is added or removed, or the setter changes. Tron sets a variable for a child process, or removes one. A log line that a row quotes changes. A file that a row names is moved or renamed. The last two cases change no variable, so an agent that follows the AGENTS.md sentence does not open the rules for such a PR. Also, "which changes need a row" does not match the rules. The rules say which changes need an update of the file, and rule 7 says which variables need no row.
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md lines 29-33: "A PR that adds, renames, or removes an environment variable, or changes how one is parsed, its default, or its effect, updates README.env-vars.md in the same PR. Its Rules for developers say which changes need a row and where the row goes." README.env-vars.md lines 81-86 hold the 4 other cases: "It adds or removes a reader of an existing variable, or changes who sets a variable." "It makes Tron set a variable for a child process or a library, or remove one from the environment of a child process." "It changes a log line that a row of this file quotes." "It moves or renames a file that a row names." The file name and the anchor in AGENTS.md are correct: README.env-vars.md exists and "#rules-for-developers" matches the heading at line 71.
findings.fix: Replace the paragraph in AGENTS.md with: "A PR that adds, renames, or removes an environment variable, or changes how one is parsed, its default, its effect, or what reads or sets it, updates [README.env-vars.md](README.env-vars.md) in the same PR. So does a PR that moves a file or changes a log line that a row of that file names. Its [Rules for developers](README.env-vars.md#rules-for-developers) list every case and say where a row goes." Wrap the lines at 80 columns as in the rest of AGENTS.md.

findings.where: README.env-vars.md lines 92-96 (rule 1 of "How to write a row", first case) against the row MIXTRAL_PATH at line 674 (section 4.1)
findings.problem: The rule and one row disagree. Rule 1 says that a variable read by Rust source under rust/ goes in section 1, and that the Dice grant variables are "the one exception". rust/tokenizers/src/lib.rs reads MIXTRAL_PATH, and its row is in section 4.1. The place of the row is reasonable, because only unit tests read the name. The rule text does not allow it, and AGENTS.md sends developers to this rule to learn where a row goes.
findings.evidence: A git grep for getenv, secure_getenv, env::var and env! names under src/, h/ and rust/ gives 67 names. 66 of them have a row in section 1 or section 2.2. MIXTRAL_PATH is the only other name. rust/tokenizers/src/lib.rs reads it at lines 989, 1098 and 1171. All three reads are inside the module `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, which starts at line 982. The row at line 674 names "Rust unit tests of the `hf_tokenizers_ffi` crate" as a reader.
findings.fix: In lines 95-96, replace the sentence "The Dice grant variables of section 2.2 are the one exception: Dice sets them, and a person does not." with: "There are two exceptions. Dice sets the Dice grant variables of section 2.2, and a person does not. A variable that only a unit test inside this source reads, for example in a Rust `#[cfg(test)]` module, goes in section 4. `MIXTRAL_PATH` is such a variable."

findings.where: changelog.d/ (the staged change holds no fragment). Rules: changelog.d/README.md lines 3-12 and 30-32
findings.problem: The staged change adds a reference document for support engineers and no changelog fragment. changelog.d/README.md calls a change notable when someone who installs Tron or serves models with it would notice, and it lists the scope `docs`. CHANGELOG.md holds a precedent for a new root README. The fragment name needs the pull request number, so the fragment cannot be staged before the draft pull request exists. No CI check requires a fragment, so nothing fails without it.
findings.evidence: changelog.d/README.md line 10: "Name it `<PR>.<section>.md` ... Open the pull request to get its number, then push the fragment." Lines 30-32 list the scopes, `docs` among them. CHANGELOG.md line 383, under "### Added": "- docs: List third-party components and licenses in [SBOM](README.sbom.md)." git grep for "changelog" in .github/workflows, bin/ci, lefthook.yml, GNUmakefile and flake.nix finds no check. The existing fragment changelog.d/5429.added.md shows the link form `(../doc/...)`.
findings.fix: After the draft pull request has its number N, push the file changelog.d/N.added.md with this one line: "- docs: List environment variables in [README.env-vars.md](../README.env-vars.md). (#N)". With a 4-digit N the line has 67 characters without the link target, and the limit is 80 characters. If the team counts the document as internal, say so in the pull request description and add no fragment.

findings.where: README.env-vars.md lines 53-57 ("The columns mean") against the 10 tables of section 7
findings.problem: Each table of section 7 has 5 columns: Variable, Defined by, Tron, Where, What Tron does with it. The list "The columns mean" has no entry for "What Tron does with it". It explains the column "Tron" with nearly the same words: "what Tron code does with the name". Also, 13 rows say that Tron code removes the name, and their "Tron" cell shows only Reads, Sets, or Reads and sets. The text does not say that Unsets appears only when Tron neither reads nor sets the name. All 144 "Tron" cells do hold one of the four allowed values.
findings.evidence: Header of the tables at lines 916, 941, 968, 1029, 1049, 1060, 1073, 1082, 1091, 1099. Rows that name a removal without "Unsets": GITHUB_JOB (950), GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT (955), GITHUB_RUN_ID (956), MAKECMDGOALS (1001), MAKEFLAGS (1002), MAKELEVEL (1003), PYTEST_ADDOPTS (1033), PYTHONPATH (1042), PYTHONWARNINGS (1044), ALL_PROXY (1062), all_proxy (1063), NO_PROXY (1068), no_proxy (1069). Example, line 1003: MAKELEVEL shows "Reads", and its "Where" cell says "`bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` removes it for `make` commands that it starts."
findings.fix: Replace the bullets for "Tron" and "Where" (lines 54-57) with three bullets: "- **Tron** (section 7): one of *Reads*, *Sets*, *Reads and sets* or *Unsets*. *Reads*: Tron code reads the name. *Sets*: Tron code sets it, for itself or for a child process. *Unsets*: Tron code only removes it from the environment of a child process. When Tron code also reads or sets the name, the cell shows that, and the Where cell names the removal." "- **Where** (section 7): the Tron files that read, set or unset the name." "- **What Tron does with it** (section 7): how Tron code uses the name."

findings.where: README.env-vars.md rule 2 at line 105 against the tables of sections 5.4, 6.5, 7.4 and 7.6
findings.problem: Rule 2 says: "Keep the rows of each table sorted by name. Ignore upper and lower case." It does not say where an underscore sorts. All 48 variable tables are sorted when the names are compared in lower case, so there is no row to move. A check that folds to upper case, such as `sort -f` with LC_ALL=C, reports 5 pairs in 4 tables as out of order. A later contributor can then reorder correct rows.
findings.evidence: My script found 0 unsorted pairs with lower-case comparison. With upper-case comparison it found: `__NIX_USERNAME` before `CLANG_RESOURCE_DIR` and `CMAKE_C_COMPILER` before `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` (5.4, lines 791-794), `SLICE_REFRESH_RUN_URL` before `SLICE_REFRESH_RUNNER_CLASS` (6.5, lines 897-898), `PY_COLORS` before `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` (7.4, lines 1032-1033), `http_proxy` before `HTTPS_PROXY` (7.6, lines 1065-1066).
findings.fix: Replace line 105 with: "2. Keep the rows of each table sorted by name. Compare the names in lower case, character by character. An underscore then sorts before a letter: `PY_COLORS` comes before `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`."

findings.where: README.env-vars.md rule 5 at lines 118-119, and the size of the whole file
findings.problem: Rule 5 protects each row against the line limit of GitHub code search (1,024 characters). The same GitHub list has a file limit: code search excludes files over 350 KiB. The file has 307,023 bytes (299.8 KiB, 85.7% of the limit). 51,377 bytes are left, which is about 76 rows of the mean row length of 676 characters. Past the limit, code search finds no row of the file. Nothing in the file warns about this limit.
findings.evidence: ls -l on README.env-vars.md gives 307,023 bytes, and 350 KiB is 358,400 bytes. GitHub Docs, "About GitHub Code Search", section "Limitations": "Empty files and files over 350 KiB are excluded" and "Lines over 1,024 characters long are truncated" (https://docs.github.com/en/search-github/github-code-search/about-github-code-search, read 2026-11-22). The mean length of the 405 variable rows is 676 characters (my script).
findings.fix: Add two sentences to rule 5 after line 119: "Keep the whole file under 350 KiB (358,400 bytes). GitHub code search excludes larger files." No row needs a change for this pull request.

notes: Short version: 1 must-fix, 3 should-fix and 7 optional findings. The must-fix is a false statement in "How to check this file": the commands print SELF_DIR. No CI check or hook that reads the three files fails, by my reading of their source. Limits of this review: I ran no repository script, no build and no test. I read the source of the checks and repeated their logic with read-only git commands. I changed no file in the checkout. Checks that passed. (1) Old file name: "README.environment.md" has 0 hits in the three staged files and 0 hits in the other tracked files. (2) Links: README.env-vars.md has 23 links, README.md 23 and AGENTS.md 19. Every target file exists and every anchor matches a heading, also "README.env-vars.md#rules-for-developers". (3) Section numbers: 25 references in the text (for example "section 2.2", "section 2.4", "Sections 4.1 to 4.5", "4.6 Fixture variables", "6.4 Step values") all match the headings and their content. (4) Tables: 52 tables with 438 rows. No table is empty. No heading lacks content. Every row has the column count of its header. Every repository path in backticks exists among the tracked files. (5) Row rules over the 405 variable rows: the longest row has 999 characters, so 0 rows pass 1,000 (35 rows have 990 or more, so an added word can pass the limit). All tables and both name lists (4.6, 6.4) are sorted in lower case. "For" holds 19 Operators and 51 Developers and no other value. Every "Values and default" cell holds "Unset:". No cell is empty. The "Tron" cells hold 55 Reads and sets, 53 Sets, 30 Reads and 6 Unsets. No cell holds a line number of the form file.ext:123. The 3 matches of that pattern are host:port values. The words reviewer, audit, hint and agent appear only as code names or as a description of code: paths under .agents/, the hook name agent-guidance, AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY, PAUSE_HINT, TRON_REQUIRE_CLOSURE_AUDIT, SLICE_REFRESH_REVIEWERS, and "prints a hint" in line 895. I report none of them. (6) Words: no British spelling, no word "flag" outside code, and no "TRON" as a project name, in README.env-vars.md and in the added lines of README.md and AGENTS.md. (7) Duplicates: 529 names (405 rows and 124 names in the lists of 4.6 and 6.4). No name has two entries. (8) CI and hooks. Two checks read these files. First, the whitespace check (lefthook.yml lines 15-28, flake.nix lines 2303-2309): "git diff --cached --check" exits with status 0 against HEAD and against the empty tree for the three files. Second, the agent-guidance check (bin/ci/lint-agent-guidance.py lines 323-342, run by lefthook.yml lines 252-270 and flake.nix lines 2441-2442): it tests that each relative link in AGENTS.md points to an existing path and it ignores the anchor. Both new links point to README.env-vars.md, which is tracked. CLAUDE.md still holds exactly "@AGENTS.md". bin/ci/test-lint-agent-guidance.py uses only temporary directories. "make lint-notes" reads doc/*.md and a fixed file list, not the root README files. The local pre-commit hook agent-guidance runs for this commit because AGENTS.md is staged, and it needs python3 with PyYAML and markdown-it-py. (9) README.md lines 70, 503-523 and 574-588 name POS_NR_HUGEPAGES, the REMOTE_BUILD_* variables and SYSTEM_CONFIG. Their statements agree with the rows. The row POS_NR_HUGEPAGES names the second meaning that README.md gives. (10) The baseline line is correct: commit 7eddde7895 has the date 2026-11-21 and is the HEAD of the branch. Small wording points that I did not list as findings: line 336 calls the group of section 2.4 "the Dice service variables" and the heading says "Dice test overrides". The closing sentence of 6.4 says "The workflow file explains each one", and 2 of its 7 lines name a script.
